intro_line: Changchun: wide Japanese-planned avenues, deep winter cold, and a rich rail history.
intro: Changchun rewards visitors with compact squares, hearty northeastern food, and easy rail links across the region. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
transit_facts: Metro and light rail: 6 lines (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8) cover many central areas; T-Union card works.
Trams 54 and 55 run in the west; fare ¥2, route 55 ends at West station.
Buses are extensive and cost about ¥2; Chinese reading helps a lot.
Taxis are cheap and easy; flag fall ¥5 plus ¥1 fuel surcharge.
Ride apps: Didi works; local apps may need Chinese registration.
Walking is fine May to mid-November; cycling is risky in traffic.

airports.name: Longjia International Airport
airports.note: Main airport, about 32 km east of the centre.

options.note: Longjia rail station links to the terminal; no trains roughly 8pm-7am.
Include toll; drivers may ask for at least ¥100 from the airport.

place_landmarks: Museum of the Imperial Palace of Manchukuo
